links.reason: The convention of pallor on parting is shared, but the epic verse only asks வஞ்சமாங் கொலோ ('could it be deceit?'), a question, not a proof, and nothing in it says a wife who knows her husband safe does not pale. The Kural's pallor is the woman's own, so 'misjudged from outside' is the marker's gloss.

Marusi's விஞ்சையர் விச்சையாலே விழுமியர்... மனிதரே matches 972's birth alike, worth by work, so the link is real. But the verse says nothing of a marriage, so 'the reason a marriage across a divide may go ahead' is read in from the plot, and the lore/செய்தொழில் equation is the note's.

A patikam summary and a later scene are joined only by the cousin's marriage. 2133 shows a look (நோக்கினாள்); nothing in it makes the marriage 'serve the war' or shows a council, so teaches is read from plot, not the Tamil.

Both show a wife's sulk, but 1018 calls her பெண்டிரைப் பொறாது சீறுவாள், jealous even at the name of other women, which presents it as her trait and புலவி, not a 'just grievance'. The couplet's baseless suspicion is not contrasted with a true one in the Tamil.

99 gives the bride at the வேள்வி and 100 has the prince win the city for Vanaraja, so the later verse follows the earlier. Nothing says the conquest repays the gift; that obligation is the note's. This is story order, and 99 is flagged uncertain.
links.text_issue: 99 flagged uncertain; daughter's name lost from line 2

links.reason: The verse gives mantra and touch (உருவம் ஓதி... சிகழிகை யழுத்தி); it does not mention poison. 705's அருஞ்சனம் may be collyrium, not poison, and line 3 is garbled, so the pair rests on an uncertain word. The 7000 Brahmins and 'adept's power' come from outside the verse.

2466 only reports (என்ப) that the fire rises right as an omen of fortune; 551 says the sacrifice (யாகத்திற்) gives no போக்கு to release. One speaks of fortune, the other of release, so the claims are not incompatible; the note admits this in its own teaches.

Both are Gunamalai's wasting, reported by two voices, so the second repeats the first's matter. 'Grief growing in the interval' and the co-wife as the one who 'carries it' are not in the lines: 1744 is already Nandattan reporting to Civakan, and 1877 adds only the day-and-night confusion.

A king remitting dues and ending பசியும் நோயும் பகையும் illustrates கொடை and குடியோம்பல். The verse says nothing of what this costs a treasury or who gains, so teaches adds a point the Tamil lacks; the sense is flagged uncertain and the 'sixteen years' is a guess.
links.text_issue: பதிளை யாண்டை and குறுகடன் readings uncertain

links.reason: Same jester, same scene: 1576 has the mouth watering (வாயெயிறூற), 1569 the belly full of modakas. The recurrence is real but the teaches is only the shared trait; the verses are adjacent in one episode and the pairing shows no new meaning.

Both verses are the muni's account of afterlives, so there is no clash. Line 4 gives ஒருபதினொடு எழுகடல்கள் against 285's பத்தும் (with மிகை) so the comparison of length is real, but it is the same Jain scheme applied twice; the arithmetic of lines 1-3 is unresolved and 295 is flagged uncertain.

1631 reasons that if her life left her body, his would go too (காதலாளுடல் உள்ளுயிர் கைவிடின்... என்னுயிர் இறக்கும்), which is the idea of 1122, but there is no shared run of words and the body and life are not the simile's terms. So 'the couplet's settled formula' as a known saying is not shown.

யானுமலது எனதுமலது இதமுமலது extends யான் எனது of 346 by a third term, and the neighbouring Tamil gives the ascetic's reward in the dirt of deeds not clinging. The pairing teaches that the Jain verse goes past the Kural's pair, and both gains clauses are specific.

986's line 3-4 (செய்தவமுடைய காளை... இகிரி யாள்தற் கையமொன்றில்லை) reaffirms the wheel-rule that the court in 109 confirmed (உலகமெல்லாம் ஒருகுடை நீழல் காக்கும்) and supplies a cause, செய்தவம். That is a later unit answering and adding to the earlier, not mere sequence.

Both are resolves to find Civakan or die (காண்கலேமாயின்... / ஏற்றுலகடைதல்), but they are parallel resolves, not incompatible claims. Buddhisenan's aim is to kill the king and follow; Nandattan's is to find his lord. That the private vow 'brings him to the woman who can reunite them' is not in 1745.

1181 only puts the question of which kind of war (மனிதப் போரோ... தெய்வப் போரோ... இருமையின்), with no weighing of deed, self, foe and allies. The council's answer is not in the verse, so 'shows a council doing the weighing' and the foe's divine arts are supplied by the note; sense flagged uncertain.
links.text_issue: speaker identified only by his banner

links.reason: 2883 puts rule and the giving of the kingdom to a son before renouncing; Naladiyar 11's நரைவரும் என்றெண்ணி... குழவியிடத்தே துறந்தார் praises renouncing in childhood. The two give opposing answers about when renunciation should begin, and both gains clauses name specific things.

The shared image is real: உடம்பு as an ஈமம் burned by the காமக் கனல் against Pattinattar's ஈமக் கனலிலிடு விருந்து and காமக் கனலிற் கருகுஞ் சருகு. But these are not incompatible claims, and which text borrows from which is not shown, so both gains clauses are guesses.

The epic has the father give the daughter எரியழல் முன்னர் with a declared dowry, while Akananuru 86 pours water and paddy and has the kin give her. The contrast is true of the words, but that the Sangam poem 'lacks' fire or dowry is an argument from silence and 2079 is flagged uncertain.

இன்பக் கனிகள் in 289 is a plain figure for love's pleasure; 201's jackfruit and wild date is an argument against adultery. A fruit for pleasure is a common figure, and 289 has no moral weight at all, so 'opposite moral weights' is the note's invention.

670's reasoning is deeds and precedent (அன்று நாம் முயலப்பட்ட வினைகள்... மேலை வேந்தர் ஒன்றி உவப்பித்து ஆண்டது), not fear of trouble within as in 680's உள்நடுங்கல் அஞ்சி. A small king bowing is the shared outline, but 'step by step' is untrue, and 666 and 672 lie outside the verse.

Both ends are true: 1420 has the army scatter (இரிந்தது... தானையே) and 765's கூடி எதிர்நிற்கும் is the standard it fails. But the verse names no leader who 'holds' an army, so teaches adds a point from outside; the gains clauses are modest but true.

889 closes the tour (பல காட்டி... சேர்ந்தார்) that 875 opens (அறிவித்தாள்). This is the same tour in order, which the graph already records; no verse fulfils or reverses another. 'The descriptions serve the arrival' is a general remark; 875 is flagged uncertain.

298 names births ending in the cock that வதம் மருவி and then Abhaya; 2133 has old deeds follow the subtle body into a new body. T saying nothing of a vow is an argument from silence, and the two are different schools' accounts of rebirth. The first beasts are unclear and 298 is flagged uncertain.

Buddhisenan's பின்றிநீங்கிற் பழி தரும்படித் தன்றியும் சாற்றுவல் is a warning of blame in retreat before more argument. 467 says deliberation must come before resolving, and does not leave a reason unstated. The pair shares only the caution; the 'cost' gained is invented.

741 values a fort for those who fear (அஞ்சித்தற் போற்றுபவர்க்கும்) and 775 says a warrior's blink is flight. They speak of different people (rulers and fighters), and 741 sets no standard against which 775 could conflict, so this is shared topic, not tension.

304 has the burning ground's deities (அணங்கு) bow at Civakan's birth; Manimekalai 6's lines ask who could be greater fools than those who revel without அறம், having seen Death heap the dead for the சுடலை. The passage is general ethics from the goddess, not Buddhist doctrine, and 304 makes no claim about providence, so no incompatible claims.

Both verses contain ஆறிலொன்று; 54 gives it as அறம் taken with அருள், and 244 puts அறநெறி for முத்தியும் செல்வமும் beside the king's sixth. The marker admits the halves of 244 are loosely joined, so 'makes it a step on the road to release' is a stretch, and 244 says nothing of sparing foes.

The sage's குடையுடை வேந்தர்களாகுவர் for those who give food sets reward as the ground of giving, while 222's மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும் ஈதலே நன்று makes giving good without it. The pair teaches a real contrast of reasons for the same act, and both gains clauses are specific.

Both use the root கடை, and Padumai's heart is the churned sea (கடைந்திடப்பட்ட நீர் மறுகு மாக்கடல்) while Civakan asks காமமே கடைகின்றது. The verb is shared, but 'lying apart on the same night' and the poet binding two laments are not in the Tamil; this is a modest echo, not a designed pairing.

1164 is Madanan's false report of killing (மார்புபோழ்ந் துருட்டி யிட்டேம்) and 2197 shows Kattiyangaran regretting that the killing failed (பிழைத்த பிழைப்பு), so a claim is met by its refutation. Type tension is wrong for two linked units; 'undone by his own lies' and 'the contest set as his trap' are not in the lines.

Both are neythal scenes of a visitor asked or refusing to stay at the shore town (தங்கினிராயின் தவறோ / தங்கின்மற்று எவனோ). They are different lovers and different poems, so 'who proposes the stay marks how far the affair has gone' is not shown by either; it is a shared motif.

106 tells the dream (வேழம்... மாலை சூட்டி) and 107 gives its பயன், a Vidyadhara king giving his daughter. The later verse reads the earlier, so this is a sign and its reading rather than bare sequence.

1152 sets aside the friends' plan and the wife's magic (விஞ்சையால் விடுத்துக்கொள்ளப் போயுயிர் வாழ்தல் வேண்டேன்) after Buddhisenan's burn-the-city plan in 1140, so one answers the other, but this is not a tension. 'Deliverance comes only from the bond he made himself' is outside both verses.

176 sends அமைச்சரை and the நாற்படை with the bride's gift, which matches படை and அமைச்சு among 381's six. That is a listing of items, and the verse does not say Udayanan had lost a state or is rebuilding one, so 'by marriage, not long building' is plot supplied by the note.

The Jina conquering the five senses (ஐம்பொறியும் அட்டு) and singing his lotus feet matches 1775's feet and ஐம்புலம் வென்று. The contrast with grace is real, but the hymn is silent on the worshipper's own task of restraint, and 1775's அன்று என்று is unclear, so the contrast is the note's.

1260 has the dancer call பொன்னினால் உடையுங் கற்பு a lie, and 371 says a harlot's love ends when the hand is empty. They are near but not the same saying (love ending vs chastity breaking), and no words are shared, so 'the very proverb' is too strong. The tension is only on a generous reading.

1119 has the groom say வழிபடுவதே சாலும் of her feet, and 1037 compares those who bow at the Jina's feet to lotuses blooming at the maiden's feet. The comparison already sits in 1037, so the groom's line repeats it, and both are flagged uncertain.
links.text_issue: 1037 lines 2-3 doubled; feet of Jina or maiden ambiguous

links.reason: Same counsel, kept away from love, with opposite grounds: K206's அமிழ்தத் தன்ன இளிவரல் against N41's carrion body. Their grounds differ but the advice agrees, so this is not a tension. The pair does teach that one counsel can rest on two views of the beloved.

182's cutting and tearing of the crocodile (குறைத்தனர் ஈர்ந்தனர்) is read as Chandramathi's fate for urging the kid-sacrifice in 137 (குறுமறி கொன்று சண்டிகை மனந்தளிர்ப்ப). The verse never names her, so the identification is outside the Tamil.

Both open with feet-worship (பாதம் பணிய / சேவடி சேர்தும்), and the lords differ (Nemi under the பிண்டி, a nameless god of gods). That the 'chosen tirthankara tells which tradition' is not shown by either verse; this is the shared convention of an invocation.

Both have the lover travelling or longing sustained by the beloved (எம் வெம் காதலி பண்பு துணை / உள்ளினும் தீராப் பெருமகிழ்). But 325 does not say remembered joy never fails, and 'puts it to a test' assumes an order of composition. Sense flagged uncertain.

1317 compares Dhumaketu to ஊழிநாள் எரியும் கூற்றமும் as a simile of fury and says a man dies when the days of his life are spent. 176 says thinking of the Lord keeps off Death's messengers. A simile for a warrior is not a claim about Death's power, so the two are not in conflict.
